tip.til: til always takes the genitive: Við viljum fara til Íslands.
landing.say: "TÖL-va": Icelandic for computer, from tala (number) and völva (seeress).
landing.pitchTitle: Built for what makes Icelandic hard
landing.casesText: Every form comes from the Database of Icelandic Morphology. Endings are color-coded by case and always labeled, and every hint says why a case is used.
landing.soundsText: hv sounds like kv, ll like tl, and vowels can be long or short. Every item gets audio with a slow option, plus IPA where it exists.
landing.soundsExample: sl is often said with a t in between: stl.
landing.bridgeText: Use the app in English or Norwegian Bokmål, read glosses in either, and spot the cognates and false friends you already know.

profile.intro: Your progress is stored on this device only. There are no accounts.
profile.dataText: Export all progress as a file, or import it on another device. Importing replaces the progress on this device.
settings.intro: Changes apply right away and are saved on this device.
settings.calmHelp: Removes scanlines, glitch, pulsing and large glows. Auto follows your device's reduced motion and contrast settings.
settings.scanHelp: The CRT effect. Reading screens always use the low setting unless you turn it off.
settings.sfxHelp: Short 8-bit chimes for answers. Off by default.

settings.strictHelp: Easy accepts missing accents as almost right. Strict counts them as wrong, because accents change words.
settings.heartsHelp: Lose a heart for each mistake. Off by default.
settings.glossHelp: Norwegian glosses appear where the data has them; otherwise English is shown.

decl.usesNote: These are the main rules; there are exceptions. Í and á take the dative for a place and the accusative for movement.

bridge.intro: Icelandic and Norwegian both grew out of Old Norse. Many words still match once you know a few spelling patterns.
bridge.patternsText: Pick a pattern to see its words. Pick it again to see all.
bridge.credit: Norwegian words and their Old Norse origins: Bokmålsordboka, Universitetet i Bergen og Språkrådet, ordbøkene.no, CC BY 4.0. Icelandic origins: Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0. The pairs are matched by a script, and each shows its evidence: an Old Norse word named by both sources, a shared loan, or only a similar form.
bridge.ev.form: Same meaning and a similar spelling. A shared origin is not confirmed by the sources.
practice.bridgeText: Icelandic words that you can guess from Norwegian, and the patterns behind them.
